title: How far does the faster tortoise walk in three quarters of an hour?
description: A faster tortoise covers two fifths of a kilometre in one hour, and the video finds the distance for three quarters of an hour with a unit square of rows and columns. Keeko then raises a hand with the doubt that the tops and the bottoms can be added.
teaching_notes: One idea: to find a fraction of a fraction, cut the fraction into equal parts first, count the small parts in the whole square, and then take as many of those parts as needed. Watch for students who add the tops and add the bottoms.

source: If Laksh's tortoise walks faster and covers 2/5 km in 1 hour, how far will it walk in 3/4 of an hour?
video_script.why: The child has cut a quarter into two equal parts and now cuts two fifths into four equal parts, then takes three of them.
video_script.substitution: Cutting two fifths into four equal parts gives two twentieths, and three of those parts make three quarters of the distance.
video_script.anchor: Laksh's faster tortoise covers two fifths of a kilometre in one hour: how far in three quarters of an hour?
video_script.wrong_move: adds the tops, three and two, and the bottoms, four and five, and gets five ninths, which is more than the distance of the whole hour
video_script.payoff_line: The tortoise walks three tenths of a kilometre in three quarters of an hour
video_script.fraction_reading: two fifths, one quarter, three quarters, two twentieths, six twentieths, three tenths, five ninths

names.Laksh: walks 3 km in 1 hour; his pet tortoise walks 1/4 km in 1 hour

maths_rules: 1/4 of 2/5: 5 rows and 4 columns make 5 × 4 = 20 equal parts, with 2 shaded, so 2/20
video_script.design: One idea: cut the fraction into equal parts, count the small parts, then take the number asked for. The unit square with five rows and four columns is the anchor and stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a line with a faster tortoise at the start and a mark at 2/5 km for 1 hour; a question mark at three quarters of an hour

marks.scene: the small title card From your book appears
marks.walk: the mark at two fifths of a kilometre is placed for one hour
marks.ask: a question mark appears at three quarters of an hour

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the tortoise of Laksh.
<bookmark mark='walk'/>The tortoise walks faster now, and covers two fifths of a kilometre in one hour.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How far will it walk in three quarters of an hour?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a unit square as the whole, cut into 5 equal rows; 2 of the rows are shaded

marks.square: a unit square appears as the whole
marks.rows: the square is cut into five equal rows

narration: <bookmark mark='square'/>Draw a unit square and take it as the whole.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>Cut it into five equal rows, and shade two rows to show two fifths.
<bookmark mark='shade'/>The shaded part is the distance of one hour.

marks.given: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the tortoise covers two fifths of a kilometre in one hour.

beats.on_screen: To find: distance in 3/4 of an hour

marks.find: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the distance in three quarters of an hour.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Step one, write the distance as a multiplication.
Three quarters of an hour means three quarters of two fifths of a kilometre.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: distance in 1/4 hour: the 2 shaded rows are cut into 4 equal parts with 4 columns; 5 rows × 4 columns = 20 equal parts; 2 parts shaded = 2/20

marks.one: the line for one quarter of an hour is written
marks.two: two parts stay shaded and 2/20 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step two, first find the distance in one quarter of an hour.
<bookmark mark='cut'/>Cut the shaded rows into four equal parts, using four columns.
<bookmark mark='twenty'/>The whole has five rows and four columns, so five times four is twenty equal parts.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Two of these parts are shaded, which is two twentieths.

marks.three: the line for three quarters of an hour is written

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, multiply by three to get three quarters of an hour.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Three times two is six, and the parts stay twentieths.

marks.pay: the answer stays on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Six twentieths is the same as three tenths, because we divide the top and the bottom by two.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The tortoise walks three tenths of a kilometre in three quarters of an hour.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 3/4 × 2/5 = 5/9 is written and crossed out; 5/9 is drawn longer than 2/5; the unit square with 20 parts is shown again

marks.fix: 5/9 is drawn longer than 2/5 and the line is crossed out
marks.rule: the shaded small parts and all the small parts glow in turn

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is five ninths of a kilometre.
Keeko added the tops, three and two, and added the bottoms, four and five.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But five ninths is more than two fifths.
Three quarters of an hour cannot go further than the whole hour.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Count the shaded small parts, and count all the small parts in the square.
